knowledge:
- key_parameters: aData=The input data in matrix format with rows denoting features and columns denoting samples ;; vec_trt=A vector for group notation where "1" denotes the treatment group and "0" denotes the control group ;; repetition=The number of resamples (permutations or bootstraps) to perform ;; alpha=The significance level ;; aContrast=A contrast vector for pairwise comparisons in RBM_F (e.g., c("X1-X0", "X2-X1", "X2-X0"))
- alternatives: lmFit and eBayes functions from the limma package, which are used internally by RBM to compute the initial moderated t-statistics
- when_to_use: Use this package when analyzing differential expression in two-color microarrays, RNA-Seq, or DNA methylation datasets where a resampling-based empirical Bayes approach (permutation or bootstrap) is preferred over standard parametric assumptions to control false positives
- pitfalls: Ensure that the group notation vector matches the columns of the input data matrix. For RBM_F, users must prepend an extra "X" before the group labels in the contrast vector (e.g., "X1-X0" to compare group 1 and group 0). The package outputs raw permutation and bootstrap p-values, which should be post-processed using p.adjust for multiple testing correction.

workflows.name: two_group_comparison
workflows.intent: Identify differentially expressed or methylated features between two groups using resampling-based moderated t-statistics.
input: ovarian_cancer_methylation.csv (DNA methylation profile matrix with features as rows and samples as columns)
label.csv (vector of group assignments, e.g., 0 for control and 1 for treatment)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the RBM package and the input dataset ;; 2. Extract the data matrix and define the group label vector ;; 3. Run RBM_T to compute moderated t-statistics, permutation p-values, and bootstrap p-values ;; 4. Adjust the resulting p-values using the Benjamini-Hochberg method ;; 5. Identify and print significant features based on adjusted p-values
workflows.code:
library(RBM)
data(ovarian_cancer_methylation)
summary(ovarian_cancer_methylation)
ovarian_cancer_data <- ovarian_cancer_methylation[, -1]
label <- c(1, 1, 0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0)
diff_results <- RBM_T(aData=ovarian_cancer_data, vec_trt=label, repetition=100, alpha=0.05)
summary(diff_results)
sum(diff_results$ordfit_pvalue<=0.05)
sum(diff_results$permutation_p<=0.05)
sum(diff_results$bootstrap_p<=0.05)

ordfit_adjp <- p.adjust(diff_results$ordfit_pvalue, "BH")
sum(ordfit_adjp<=0.05)
perm_adjp <- p.adjust(diff_results$permutation_p, "BH")
sum(perm_adjp<=0.05)
boot_adjp <- p.adjust(diff_results$bootstrap_p, "BH")
sum(boot_adjp<=0.05)

diff_list_perm <- which(perm_adjp<=0.05)
diff_list_boot <- which(boot_adjp<=0.05)
sig_results_perm <- cbind(ovarian_cancer_methylation[diff_list_perm, ], diff_results$ordfit_t[diff_list_perm], diff_results$permutation_p[diff_list_perm])
print(sig_results_perm)
sig_results_boot <- cbind(ovarian_cancer_methylation[diff_list_boot, ], diff_results$ordfit_t[diff_list_boot], diff_results$bootstrap_p[diff_list_boot])
print(sig_results_boot)

workflows.name: multi_group_comparison
workflows.intent: Identify differentially expressed or methylated features across multiple groups using pairwise contrasts and resampling-based F-tests.
input: normdata_F.csv (matrix of normalized expression values with features as rows and samples as columns)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the RBM package and prepare the input data matrix, multi-group design vector, and contrast vector ;; 2. Run RBM_F to compute moderated statistics, permutation p-values, and bootstrap p-values for the specified contrasts ;; 3. Adjust the resulting p-values for each contrast using the Benjamini-Hochberg method ;; 4. Identify significant features for each pairwise contrast
workflows.code:
library(RBM)
normdata_F <- matrix(rnorm(1000*9,0,2), 1000, 9)
mydesign_F <- c(0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2)
aContrast <- c("X1-X0", "X2-X1", "X2-X0")

myresult_F <- RBM_F(normdata_F, mydesign_F, aContrast, 100, 0.05)
summary(myresult_F)
sum(myresult_F$permutation_p[, 1]<=0.05)
sum(myresult_F$permutation_p[, 2]<=0.05)
sum(myresult_F$permutation_p[, 3]<=0.05)

which(myresult_F$permutation_p[, 1]<=0.05)
which(myresult_F$permutation_p[, 2]<=0.05)
which(myresult_F$permutation_p[, 3]<=0.05)
    
con1_adjp <- p.adjust(myresult_F$permutation_p[, 1], "BH")
sum(con1_adjp<=0.05/3)
  
con2_adjp <- p.adjust(myresult_F$permutation_p[, 2], "BH")
sum(con2_adjp<=0.05/3)

con3_adjp <- p.adjust(myresult_F$permutation_p[, 3], "BH")
sum(con3_adjp<=0.05/3)

which(con2_adjp<=0.05/3)

which(con3_adjp<=0.05/3)
